catalogue.note: The redesigned Academy. Drawn in Figma at 0.75 of real size (270×600; instances carry scaleFactor 0.75): built at 360×800 with every value divided by 0.75 (type 14/13/12/11/10, margins 24, thumbnails 104×96 with 16 radius). Square-cornered: the frame’s own 12px corners are left off and the diff leaves the four corners out. Static, no scrolling: the scroll area (270×406.5 in Figma) does not clip there, so the 816-tall body runs on under the navbar, which covers it from 702; built as the frame shows it, and the part that lies wholly under the navbar and bottom bar (the rest of “It’s dry!” is there, the Older section and its four articles are not built). The four pictures are the files Figma holds, unchanged, cropped by CSS the way Figma crops them (fill, centred): the Bitcoin banner is 1500×500 and shows at 2.6×, the three thumbnails at 3.1× to 3.5×. The first article is a plain 234×186 frame, not auto-layout: its picture is 228 wide and starts 0.8 in, and its copy block starts 1 above the picture’s foot (Figma units); kept. Each thumbnail picture sits 0.375 left of its slot in the component; kept. The search box is the orange gradient at 8% with a 1px inside stroke of the same gradient at 8%; its clear icon is in the file at opacity 0 and keeps its room. The three-line summaries are cut by Figma with an ellipsis; CSS line-clamp cuts at the same word. Of the diff, half is inside the four pictures (Figma’s resampling against Chrome’s; 3.06% outside them). Status bar, bottom bar and every icon are Figma’s SVG export of the vectors, unchanged. Type is live Satoshi from the files on this Mac, embedded whole. Figma snaps each text baseline to a whole pixel at its own 0.75 scale and Chrome floors its own at this one: the type styles where the two land apart carry the difference as a sub-pixel offset, so at 3× every string sits on Figma’s baseline (0px off, all strings measured) and at 1× within a third of a pixel, except 16px labels, which sit two thirds high. What is left in the diff is glyph and curve antialiasing; flat fills match exactly.
